gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-nokora: Heavy-metal presence in a lowercase, all one stroke width. Nokora then spreads a dark, sturdy sans line beneath, its s never pinching, while Edo SZ plays the monument and Nokora does the steady talking.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic has a welcoming opening in its c and capitals barely taller than the lowercase. And Edo SZ, with its uniform lines in uppercase, gives that quiet body a firm, cast-metal foil to read against.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans: Cast-iron lettering, drawn in one stroke width. Noto Sans fills most of its letter height with lowercase body and a wide c, so paragraphs run smoothly under Edo SZ's heavier, monumental heading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam reads with curve endings kept well apart and tall, full lowercase shapes. But Edo SZ is the one for plain, unshaded lines that never swell, while the body font handles the sustained reading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unj: Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined leaves generous gaps where curves meet stems. Edo SZ holds a technical-pen steadiness above it, so keep the body size modest and let the heading carry the weight.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-anatolian: Edo SZ traces every letter in a line of constant weight. It excels at monument-like presence, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs, with outward-pointing terminals and a high x-height, is better at quietly carrying text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic opens its small letters wide and stands tall on a pronounced x-height, reading crisply throughout. Add Edo SZ's unmodulated line and the pair's strongest quality is its clear, drawn-wire contrast.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Wire-thin strokes, cast-iron attitude. Edo SZ is best at that monumental, constant-weight display, while Noto Sans Armenian, with tall, full c, s and z, is best at sitting comfortably in running text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Straight-edged and stately, Edo SZ moves stems and arcs in lockstep, a bold and classic look up top. Noto Sans Avestan keeps its curve tips apart and its x-height tall, so it sits cleanly below.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Professional in tone, Noto Sans Balinese gives every curved glyph a breathing space and keeps its ascenders short. And over a longer passage, that steadiness lets Edo SZ's bent-straw lines stay the one showy thing.
